what_its_for: Tremelimumab-actl is a cancer medicine (immunotherapy) used along with another medicine called durvalumab to treat a type of liver cancer called hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that cannot be removed by surgery. It helps your immune system find and fight cancer cells.
how_to_take: This medicine is given by a nurse or doctor through an IV (intravenous) line directly into your vein. Each infusion takes about 60 minutes. You will receive this at a clinic or hospital — never at home on your own. You will likely receive durvalumab at the same appointment.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your body weight. Tremelimumab-actl is typically given as a single dose on Day 1 of your treatment, along with durvalumab. After that first dose, only durvalumab continues on a regular schedule every 4 weeks. Always follow the schedule your doctor gives you.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an infusion appointment, call your doctor or cancer care team right away to set up a new appointment as soon as possible. Do not try to give yourself this medicine at home.
storage: You do not need to store this medicine at home. Your healthcare team handles all storage and preparation at the clinic or hospital.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor before starting treatment if you take any vitamins, supplements, or other medicines including herbal products. Avoid starting new medicines without checking with your doctor first. Do not get any live vaccines (such as live flu vaccine, shingles vaccine, or yellow fever vaccine) while on this treatment without asking your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you notice any of the following — these can be signs of serious immune-related side effects: skin rash, blistering, or peeling; severe diarrhea or stomach pain; yellowing of skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine; coughing, shortness of breath, or chest pain; confusion, memory problems, or severe headache; muscle weakness or pain; vision changes; unusual weight gain or loss; or severe fatigue. Also report any fever, chills, or signs of infection right away. These side effects can happen during treatment or weeks to months after your last dose.
when_it_works: Immunotherapy medicines like this one can take time to work. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular scans and blood tests. Some patients see improvement within a few months, but results vary from person to person. Do not stop treatment or miss appointments without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant, as it can harm your unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after your last dose. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 3 months after your last dose. Older adults: This medicine can be used in older adults, but side effects should be monitored closely. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been established.
